newsitem.title: USA: Baxter Q4, 1996 revenues cut by currency.
newsitem.headline: Baxter Q4, 1996 revenues cut by currency.

text.p: Baxter International Inc said foreign exchange effects reduced sales by about $30 million in the fourth quarter and by about $108 million in 1996.
Non-U.S. sales comprise more than 50 percent of the Deerfield, Ill.-based company's total revenues.

The healthcare products maker reported quarterly sales of $1.49 billion, up 10 percent from a year ago. That growth rate would have been 12 percent without currency translations, said Baxter chief financial officer Harry Kraemer.
Sales for 1996 were $5.43 billion, up eight percent. Without currencies, that rate would have been 10 percent.
"Even though our sales came in $108 million less, we hit our earnings commitment," Kraemer said.
Baxter reported fourth-quarter profits of $0.58 per share on an operating basis, up from $0.54 per share a year ago and ahead of the First Call consensus estimate by a penny.

After closing its $623-million acquisition of Switzerland's Immuno International AG in mid-1997, Baxter expects as much as 60 percent of sales and 75 percent of profits to come from outside the United States.
